s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, ulcerative, purpuric skin lesion with rapid growth and extension
salient_findings: Enlarging purpuric patch on the left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
key_facts: Lesion first developed in March 2014
Rapid growth and extension occurred in June 2014
Lesion is 30 × 25-cm in size
Centrally eroded purpuric plaque
No evidence of lymphadenopathy
Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes
Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors
No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases on CT scan

differentials: Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine involvement (CLIPPERS) syndrome
per_call: Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine involvement (CLIPPERS) syndrome

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and extension of a purpuric lesion with central ulceration, strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors, and cells staining positively with CD31

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, and presence of slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes in the dermis

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Centrally eroded purpuric plaque with peripheral reddish-purple patches and papules, and presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes in the dermis

shortlist.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesion with rapid growth and extension, and presence of plump oval cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules, and presence of cells staining positively with CD31

raw.rationale: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes, cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, and strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors, along with rapid growth and central ulceration, are characteristic features of angiosarcoma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically associated with human herpesvirus 8 and more commonly found in immunocompromised patients, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a solitary, targetoid lesion, which does not match the large, multifocal nature of the lesion described.

rejected.label: Epithelioid hemangioma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solitary, well-circumscribed lesion, which does not match the large, multifocal nature of the lesion described.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Although it can have similar histological features, the clinical presentation and rapid growth pattern are more suggestive of angiosarcoma.
